pull.title: test: fix coinbases built on arbitrary parents
pull.body:
**Problem:** Test helpers that attach active-tip templates to arbitrary parents retain the template's subsidy.
Existing reorg tests can underpay without failing, while a fork crossing a halving can overpay and fail with `bad-cb-amount`.
Bare height scripts at heights 1 through 16 also fail with `bad-cb-length`.

**Fix:** Share parent-dependent reconstruction between `BuildChain()` and `MinerTestingSetup::Block()`, deriving difficulty and coinbase fields from the actual parent.
Pad rebuilt coinbase input scripts and require coinbase-only templates so recalculating the subsidy cannot discard transaction fees.

Concept ACK

Built each commit and ran the unit tests, with a before and after of both cases against master.

Rebased to resolve conflicts and applied the review suggestions.
The block’s difficulty now uses its actual parent and timestamp, and its coinbase pays the subsidy for its resulting height.
I also added focused tests for the target and coinbase fields through the first halving.

Concept ACK

Code review 23a99695efa659ee0a0a290d4e0aa78aff8ddef9, mostly documentation feedback.

You may find the `BlockAssembler::CreateCoinbaseTx` helper in #36109 commit 902d836b75d402945ac60936f73ded056347fb57 useful. But I don't mind rebasing that PR.

comments.body:
This is an assignment rather than an adjustment, so the template's fees go with it. `MinerTestingSetup::Block` asks for its template with the mempool on, and with one transaction in it the coinbase reward comes out at 5000001000 on master and 5000000000 here, with the block still carrying that transaction.

Nothing hits it today, since the mempool is empty at every call. Would `.use_mempool = false` on that template call be simpler? It makes the site match `BuildChain`, so the overwrite is exact, and the three suites stay green with it.
Sure, added `.use_mempool = false` to `MinerTestingSetup::Block()` and asserted the shared helper receives a coinbase-only block.
Thanks! I added similar tests, with the coinbase cases combined into one fork test. I also credited you as a co-author on the commits containing them.

In 4e5aeb3535106911f8ca4e0015e70a5ea9c74330 _refactor: extract fork block reconstruction_ nit: `SwitchBlockParent(..., uint32_t new_time)` might be a better name. The caller's goal is to switch the parent and change the time. The description could then say that the block is rebuilt, and enumerate the side effects (in later commits), like modified subsidy.

In 4e5aeb3535106911f8ca4e0015e70a5ea9c74330 _refactor: extract fork block reconstruction_:

This relies on the 20-minute difficulty reset rule, which only exists on testnet3 and testnet4. Regtest doesn't have difficulty adjustment at all, but technically the same 20-minute reset rule exists. The test exploits this with a synthetic block with an `nBits` that's impossible in a "real" regtest chain.

In other words: please document this.

I'm also worried that it's a bit brittle to rely on, since we could remove the 20-minute reset rule on regtest, but I suppose we're never going to touch that consensus code.

In 9312297e159c6b3aa5ff0526ef104a4006f8fe5c _test: derive fork subsidy from parent_: let's document the reason for this restriction, so anyone who needs to relax it will know what to pay attention to.

In 9312297e159c6b3aa5ff0526ef104a4006f8fe5c _test: derive fork subsidy from parent_: this might be a good time to give `MinerTestingSetup::Block` a quick doc:

```cpp
/**
 * Prepare a coinbase-only block extending prev_hash, which need not be the active tip.
 * The coinbase has a unique zero-value output and a reward output spendable with OP_TRUE.
 * Call FinalizeBlock() after any further edits to update commitments, mine the block,
 * and submit its header.
 */
```
